title: Ghost-drift detection + synthesized eval suite for embedding + reranker stability
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description: Problem: We occasionally observe silent quality regressions after seemingly innocuous config or runtime changes (quantization toggles, kernel swap, batch scheduling). These regressions do not always show up in live traffic alerts because they alter relative scores or neighbor order subtly — a phenomenon we are calling 'ghost drift'. Goal: build an offline synthesized evaluation harness and automated detectors that (1) surface ghost-drift events tied to config/model changes, (2) produce explainable signal (which cohort / PCP metrics shifted), and (3) gate risky rollouts with automated rollbacks or canary holdouts.
background: Existing embedding/rerank quality playbooks target cohort drift and delta scorecards, but they miss low-amplitude reordering and top-K instability that can still materially affect downstream UX. Ghost-drift is most common when we alter low-level execution (quantize to 4-bit, swap CUDA/ROCm kernels, change continuous-batching thresholds) or when reranker logits normalization changes. We need a repeatable, offline signal that ties config diffs to measurable quality changes for recall/precision and ranking stability.
deliverables: Synthesized probe corpus generator (span/paraphrase/noise variants) with labeled relevance anchors
Offline evaluation harness that computes: Top-K recall, MRR, Kendall tau, neighbor-stability, embedding-norm distribution shifts, and cohort-wise precision@k
Config-diff runner that compares baseline vs candidate under identical seed and batching conditions and emits a drift score + diagnostic table
Alerting thresholds and gating rules integrated with rollouts (canary hold, auto-rollback)
Runbook documenting triage steps and mitigation paths, plus a dashboard for triage investigations
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness can run end-to-end on PR-level builds and produce a JSON artifact with metrics and per-cohort diffs
Detects injected low-amplitude ordering perturbations (synthetic test set) with >90% sensitivity at the configured threshold
DRIFT signal explains which config keys (quantize_bits, batch_window_ms, kernel_override) correlate with regression in 80% of seeded experiments
Integration with rollout system: if drift_score > threshold, canary is held and a label is attached to the rollout event
Runbook validated with a tabletop exercise and two simulated incidents documented in the ticket comments
implementation_steps: Design synthetic probe taxonomy: anchor (gold document), paraphrase variants, entity masking, typos/noise, adversarial near-duplicates
Implement probe generator service (python) with deterministic seeding and export to parquet/ndjson
Extend offline eval runner: add neighbor-stability (percentage of top-10 neighbors preserved), kendall-tau, embedding-norm histogram KL divergence
Add a lightweight config-diff runner that applies the exact same request batching/replay seed across baseline and candidate containers
Hook output artifacts into CI and a short-lived S3 location; post metrics to dashboard via ingestion job
Create gating logic in rollout control plane: evaluate artifact, compute drift_score, emit advisory or block
Author runbook and validate with simulated regressions (quantize-to-4bit, kernel-swap)
metrics_and_thresholds: drift_score (composite) = weighted(sum of normalized metric deltas): default threshold = 0.12
top-10 neighbor-stability: alert if drop > 7% absolute
Kendall tau: alert if tau < 0.88 vs baseline
embedding-norm KL divergence: alert if KL > 0.05 for primary production cohort
cohorts_and_probes: long-tail technical docs (long queries, sparse lexical overlap)
multi-lingual anchors (EN/FR/JP) - to detect quantization language regressions
paraphrase pairs for semantic recall tests
near-duplicate adversarial set for reranker robustness
runbook_summary: If drift_score breaches threshold: 1) Pause canary and tag rollout, 2) Run automated diagnostic artifact and compare per-cohort diffs, 3) If a single config key correlates (>0.6 Pearson) with the metric delta, revert that key; otherwise open incident and escalate to runtime team. Notify PM/SEs and attach eval artifact and PR link.
risks_and_open_questions: How to balance sensitivity vs false positives for low-volume cohorts (we may need cohort-weighted thresholds)
Edge-case: runtime non-determinism due to different BLAS / kernel scheduling might create noise—need robust seed and environment pinning
Cost: running full synthetic suite for every PR may be expensive—consider cheap quick-checks vs full-scan cadence
